corrections.found_by: the B0d authoring pass, before any hand-rendering was written
corrections.what: Added the `>=` and `<=` rows and the `operator_runs` inventory. The lexicon digest is re-recorded in experiments/foreign_voice_prereg.json with a dated correction; rule R and the frozen parser are byte-unchanged.
why: The first version of this file had rows for `≥` and `≤` and none for the
ASCII spellings `>=` and `<=`, which the residue also carries -- 55
statements and 13 statements of the eligible set respectively.
The constructive coverage check did not catch it because the check was
at the CHARACTER level: `>` is a row and `=` is a row, so `>=` reports
no leftover character while the renderer would say `is greater than
equals` and the inverse would hand the pinned binary `> =`. That is the
same shape as v0.18's commit 8910138 -- a fluent sentence that re-reads
as something else -- arriving through a check that looked at the wrong
granularity rather than through a missing check.
Corrected in the table AND in the check: `operator_runs` pins every
maximal operator run in the eligible set, so coverage is now asserted
over tokens.
Recorded here and dated rather than folded into the preregistration
commit, because a silently-fixed prereg artifact is worth less than a
dated one (v0.18's own rule, imported).
Consequence for B0d, stated because it matters: the id-selection rule is
seeded from THIS file's digest, so the correction moves the hundred
drawn statements. The draw had not been taken when the correction
landed, and the sealed renderings are authored against the corrected
draw. A correction taken AFTER a draw would need the draw re-taken and
both recorded.

corrections.what: The precedence reading rule is replaced: rendering is now CANONICAL rather than carried, per data/foreign_voice/grouping.json. No row, phrase or token changes -- the table itself is byte-identical in every section.
what_this_costs_and_who_pays_it: The emitted grammar changes, so EVERY covered surface is regenerated -- 435 of 2,313 actually move.

B0d's sealed hundred move with them: 15 of the 100 change and 85 stay byte-identical. Those 15 are re-authored by hand and re-sealed in a dated amendment; the other 85 must still match the v0.19 seal, and G2 asserts both halves.

This file's digest moves, which moves every seeded sample in the cycle. B0d's pool is grammar-independent so its seed pin survives -- recorded as a PARENT-COMMIT-DERIVED CONSEQUENCE rather than a transcribed constant. C-V4's three grammar-dependent pools do not survive, and the drawn id lists are pinned instead (cv4_replay_ids.json).
why: v0.19 fired every gate and voided on C-V4.drop_group at 0.80 against a 0.90 floor, for one mechanical reason: deleting a semantically redundant bracket changes the sentence and not the term. The carried-precedence rule is what made those redundant brackets constructible.

A measured bound is adequate for a number in an artifact and inadequate for a SERVED surface. Once the line is wired a reader is handed one sentence with no way to know a differently-bracketed one would have certified identically, and the bound lives in a file they are not reading.
So the repair is structural elimination, not a tighter bound. G1b tested every one of the 5,228 surviving canonical grouping pairs by deleting it: 5,228 detected, zero blind.

constructive_check: Every one of the 2,319 oracle-eligible statements was tokenized under R
with exactly this table's tokens, longest first, the identifier grammar of
rule_r.json and the registered numeral pair. Leftover: ONE construct -- the
coercion arrow, 7 runs across 4 statements, which has a refusal row above.
Nothing else in the eligible set is outside this table.
This is the whole-table check v0.18's `head_coverage` block does for the
realization lexicon, done constructively rather than by head census,
because this dialect's vocabulary is closed and small enough to enumerate
`operator_runs` below is the second half of that check and the half the
first version of this file did not have. A character-level sweep reports
no leftover for `>=` -- because `>` and `=` are BOTH rows -- while the
renderer would emit `is greater than equals` and the inverse would hand
the pinned binary `> =`, which is not a term at all. The runs are
enumerated so the check is about TOKENS rather than characters.

identifiers.note: All opaque variable names, all erased to `variable <index>` by the slot marker; none of them needs a row.

note: One lean_workbook statement carries a 433-digit integer, which is outside
scripts/numeral_words' registered domain (abs < 10^15) and refuses as
whose canonical decimal spellings are `23.5` and `39.5`; the numeral
pair is exact rather than approximately exact, so it cannot reproduce a
trailing zero, and `23.50` and `23.5` are DIFFERENT `OfScientific`
terms to the elaborator. That statement refuses as
`noncanonical_numeral` rather than round-tripping to a term the corpus
did not write. Both are register entries.

operator_runs_note: Every maximal run of non-identifier, non-digit, non-space characters in
the 2,319 rule-R surfaces, with its occurrence and statement counts. Each
run must decompose under longest-first munch into rows of this table; the
only exception is the coercion arrow, which has a refusal row. Pinning the
runs means a NEW run shape -- a dialect construct nobody expected, or a
corpus that grew one -- turns a test red instead of rendering to something
the inverse cannot say. `.` is the decimal point of the 34 decimal
literals; the registered numeral pair owns it, not this table.

naming_conventions: Every phrase is lowercase ASCII words separated by single spaces.
The connectives read as sentence glue rather than as symbol names -- `and
also`, `or else`, `implies that`, `exactly when`, `it fails that` -- because
the surface has to be one readable sentence for C-V3's determinacy sheet to
be answerable at all, and because a phrase like `logical and` would put the
word `and` in a position where L1 has to work harder than it needs to.
The two binder phrases share a first word (`for every` / `for some`) and the
two `it ...` connectives share theirs; both pairs differ at the second word,
so L1 holds with room to spare. This is checked by the loader, not by the
`divided by` rather than `over`, and `minus` rather than `negative`, because
`over` and `negative` are both words the registered numeral pair emits and
L2 would refuse the table at load. The gate caught both spellings during
authoring, which is the gate working.

purpose: The trusted half of the foreign-voice gate (design 3.1). Each row maps one
constructor of the FOREIGN DIALECT -- a binder, a connective, a relation, an
operator, a type name or a grouping mark -- to one English word phrase.
Forward it lexicalizes; reversed it de-lexicalizes. It is not an independent
check and is not claimed as one: its correctness is carried by review,
exactly as data/realization/lexicon.json's rows are. The independent check
is the PINNED EXTERNAL LEAN CHECKER, which this repository did not build and
which has never seen this table.
It inherits v0.18's lexicon rules WHOLE rather than restating them:
what make stage one 'a table lookup with no lookahead policy of its own'.
reading_rules: LONGEST MATCH: reading a surface left to right, take the longest phrase in
this table that matches the upcoming words; if none matches, expect a
numeral run (scripts/numeral_words). The loader makes longest match the
UNIQUE match by enforcing two properties, so the inverter needs no lookahead
policy of its own:
L1 prefix-free -- no phrase is a proper word-prefix of another phrase;
L2 numeral-disjoint -- no phrase word is a word the registered numeral
pair can emit, so one word decides numeral-run versus phrase and a
numeral run may be scanned greedily.
SLOT MARKER: the word `variable` is followed by a numeral run giving the
slot's index; the pair emits the token v<index>. Identifiers are erased to
indices ON PURPOSE and this is the one place the design's own prerequisite
pays for itself: Serialize.lean drops the `Name` field of every forallE, lam
and letE, so binder names are invisible to the identity witness by
CONSTRUCTION. Rendering a name would put information in the sentence that
the gate cannot see, which is the shape of a rendering error B1 could never
catch. The source's own identifiers are carried in the receipt's
`parameters.surface_slot_names` instead. Indices are assigned by first
occurrence in R(s), left to right.
TOKENS ARE SPACE-SEPARATED ON THE WAY BACK. The inverse writes each token
with a single space around it, so the pinned binary's lexer never has to
decide a maximal munch this table could have got wrong. `- 5` and `-5` are
the same term to Lean; `v1 0` and `v10` are not, which is exactly why the
separation is a rule and not a convenience.
NUMERALS ARE UNSIGNED. `-` is always the operator row, never part of a
literal, so the numeral pair is only ever asked for non-negative values and
its word `negative` never appears in a foreign-voice surface. This is what
removes v0.18's neg/sub collision at the root instead of legislating around
it: there is exactly one `-` row and it emits exactly one token.
PRECEDENCE IS CANONICAL, NOT CARRIED (amended 2026-08-24, correction 2
below). The rendering emits a grouping word ONLY where precedence demands
one, per data/foreign_voice/grouping.json. R(s)'s own parentheses are
re-derived rather than copied: a bracket the precedence table already
implies is not emitted, a parenthesised binder group is stripped, and an
ascription's brackets are syntax and always kept.
This REPLACES the v0.19 rule, which read 'PRECEDENCE IS CARRIED, NOT
REBUILT -- the rendering keeps R(s)'s own parentheses as `the quantity` /
`end quantity` rows and adds none'. That rule is why v0.19 voided: it let
a served sentence have a redundant-bracket variant that reads differently
and certifies identically, so a reader could not tell which one the graph
meant. C-V4.drop_group measured it at 0.80 against a 0.90 floor.
The repair is structural rather than a tighter bound. After it the variant
is not rare, it is UNGRAMMATICAL, and G1b establishes that over every one
of the 5,228 surviving grouping pairs rather than over a sample.
The rule still NEVER ADDS a bracket the source omitted: a parsing source
already follows precedence, so the canonical form can only remove. The
census publishes the per-statement delta and there is no negative bucket.
NO ROW IS IMPROVISED. A dialect construct with no row REFUSES AT THE
SURFACE, with a reason from `refusal_reasons`, and the statement lands in
the frozen register instead of in a rendering.
refusal_reasons_note: A closed vocabulary, in the spirit of v0.18's nine reasons
`interpretation_absent` are decided before rendering; the other three are
decided by this table and the registered numeral pair.

why: An up-arrow is a request to insert a coercion whose target type the
elaborator chooses. Rendering it as a word would put a phrase in the
sentence whose meaning depends on an elaboration decision the reader
cannot see, and inverting that phrase would name a coercion this table
cannot commit to. Measured on the eligible set: 9 occurrences across 4
statements. They are registered, not rendered.

relations_note: `≥` and `>=` are the SAME relation spelled two ways, and they get two rows
rather than one. The dialect really does carry both -- measured on the
eligible set, 55 statements spell it `>=` and 772 spell it `≥` -- and this
table is a token table, so a spelling the corpus uses is a row. Two rows
also make the round trip preserve the spelling, which is strictly stronger
than normalizing: the inverse hands back the same characters the corpus
The ASCII phrases are `at least equals` / `at most equals` rather than the
obvious `is greater than or equal to`, because `is greater than` is already
the `>` row and would be a proper word-prefix of it. L1 refuses that at
load, which is how the spelling was chosen.
what_is_rendered: THE RENDERER RENDERS R(s), NOT s. Correction 3 of the design is why: with
autoImplicit off -- and it must be off -- the surface handed to the oracle
has to carry an explicit binder preamble, so the sentence a reader sees is
the sentence for the statement UNDER THE DECLARED INTERPRETATION. Every
receipt carries `interpretation_shift` naming each substitution rule R
applied. A rate quoted without that field beside it is a number pretending
